checks.title: Objective lens against body width
checks.summary: The listing claims a 100 mm objective lens, and gives body dimensions of 180 × 75 × 75 mm. The lens sits across the body, whose width is at most 75 mm. The claimed lens is 1.333× that width, so the two figures cannot both be right. Listed dimensions are often inexact, so this is reported as a flag for a person to check.

steps.label: Body width available to the lens
steps.text: Body width available to the lens: 75 mm (the second-longest listed side)

steps.label: Body width with the rounding tolerance
steps.text: Body width with the rounding tolerance: 75 mm × 1.03 = 77.25 mm

assumptions: The objective lens faces along the longest side of the body, so it has to fit within the other two sides. The second-longest listed side is used as the width, which is the most lenient.
Listed dimensions are treated as rounded: a lens up to 3% wider than the listed width passes. This tolerance is a team choice, not a physical constant.
The listed dimensions are taken to describe the monocular itself, as the listing states. Because listed dimensions can be wrong, exceeding this bound is reported as a flag, not a hard result.

checks.title: Headline figures against the fine print
checks.summary: The listing gives two different figures for the same property: magnification 80 × in the headline and 12 × in the fine print (6.667×). The listing contradicts itself, which is reported as a flag.
checks.formula: ratio = headline value ÷ fine-print value; the two agree when the ratio is within the tolerance of 1

steps.label: Headline magnification divided by the fine-print value
steps.text: Headline magnification divided by the fine-print value: 80 ÷ 12 = 6.667 ×

assumptions: Two figures within 3% of each other are treated as equal. This tolerance is a team choice, not a physical constant.
